scripts.//build: TRA-3720 — this read `pnpm --filter desktop tauri build` and had NEVER run: `pnpm --filter <pkg> <name>` runs a SCRIPT called <name>, and `desktop` has no `tauri` script (its `build`/`dev` invoke the tauri BINARY). So it died in pnpm with ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT, exit 1, before any compiler started — while CLAUDE.md prescribed it as the safe `tsc -b` verify and four call sites (`//check:tra2399-controls`, `check-nonsession-rows.mjs`, `lib/tra2399-populated-gate-server.mjs`, `check-stale-js.mjs`) already read `pnpm build` as 'compile the packages to dist/'. Pointed at that meaning, which is the one the repo already had. The tauri desktop build is NOT vestigial (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/` is real) — it moved to `desktop:build`/`desktop:dev`, with the same script-vs-binary bug fixed. Deploy is unaffected: render.yaml runs `render-build`, and check-deploy-build.mjs grades only [render-build, web:build].
scripts.render-build: pnpm lint || echo '[render-build] lint reported issues (non-blocking for deploy; fix via CI/pre-commit)'; pnpm --filter @trading-app/shared build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/engine build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/backtest build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/server build && pnpm --filter desktop vite:build
scripts.//web:build: TRA-3720 — the filter was single-quoted (`'./packages/**'`). pnpm runs scripts through cmd.exe on Windows, where `'` is NOT a quote character, so pnpm received the quotes as part of the pattern, matched NOTHING, and exited 0: on any Windows checkout this segment compiled ZERO packages and reported SUCCESS. Linux (Render) uses sh and was always fine, so no deploy was ever affected — but the local pre-push check:deploy-build gate executes these segments verbatim, and it runs here. Double quotes are honoured by both shells; `@trading-app/*` selects the same five packages the glob did (agents included) — measured `Scope: 5 of 7`.
scripts.//check:new-supersession: TRA-3867 — grade the day-cell/journal supersession axis on LIVE bqb1. The raw `journalDayCellAgreementOk` is false PERMANENTLY under the TRA-3864 (b) freeze ruling (TRA-2079 refuses to move a non-zero cell), so it is not gateable; this grades `journalDayCellNoNewSupersessionOk`, which subtracts the pinned+published acknowledged set. It replays the deployed fold with a synthetic 4th divergence and requires the verdict to FLIP — a green that cannot go red is the old vacuous pass wearing a new name. Needs TRADING_ADMIN_USERNAME/PASSWORD. 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 3 BLIND.
scripts.//check:deploy-gates: TRA-2325/TRA-3699 — the discrimination suite for render-redeploy.mjs's five gates (RTH freeze, dated embargo, commit hold, stale-pin rollback, ancestry grader). Offline by default and now in pretest, because TRA-3699 shipped a fail-OPEN in gate 2 that no test would have caught: every commit-hold case INJECTS `carries`, so none of them reached the real git predicate, and the suite stayed green while a shallow graft silently lifted a hold on the live-money host. Every REFUSE case is paired with a PROCEED case differing by one variable, and the run FAILS if any verdict is never reached — a one-sided suite rubber-stamps a jammed gate. `--live` adds the network arm (real origin/main tip + bqb1's served sha); it is opt-in and NOT in pretest.
scripts.//check:deploy-gates:shallow-repro: TRA-3699 — the other half of the control, which no injected table can reach: that the real git path on a real GRAFTED repository actually produces the input that table grades. Builds the repro from scratch (clone --depth=1 via file://, THEN fetch --depth=1 each sha, so the OBJECT is present and the PATH between them is cut) and runs the shipped bytes of render-redeploy.mjs inside it. ⛔ A plain --depth=N clone is NOT the repro — there the object is simply absent and the existing gitHasCommit screen already exits BLIND for the right reason, so the arm would pass without the fix. Arm 1b re-runs the PRE-FIX bytes pinned by rev and asserts they still read CLEAR, so a fix arm cannot go green because the repro stopped biting. NOT in pretest on purpose: it needs a COMPLETE clone (it exits 2 on a shallow one), and pretest is exactly where a shallow checkout is likely.
scripts.//check:ancestry-graders:shallow-repro: TRA-3721 — the FAIL-OPEN half of the TRA-3699 ancestry sweep, on the SAME grafted state (the builder is shared: scripts/lib/shallow-graft-repro.mjs). Two graders collapsed an unreadable answer into a permission: tra2342-interlock-live-check.mjs's `--self-test` NEGATIVE CONTROL, which on a graft printed `SELF-TEST OK` without having discriminated anything — and that sentence is what licenses the checker's PASS on the `TRADIER_ENV` write and on arming live crypto — and tra2306-ceiling-grade.mjs's second TRA-2355 detector, which guarded every exit status except `1`, the one the graft lands on. Controlled in BOTH directions: every grafted arm has a complete-clone twin that must still ANSWER, because after a change that turns negatives into BLIND, `refuses everything` is the obvious way to fail. Pre-fix arms are pinned by rev (12305eba), so a fix arm cannot go green because the repro stopped biting. NOT in pretest, same reason as the TRA-3699 one: it needs a COMPLETE clone.
scripts.//check:false-red-graders:shallow-repro: TRA-3722 — the FAIL-CLOSED half of the TRA-3699 ancestry sweep, on the SAME grafted state (shared builder: scripts/lib/shallow-graft-repro.mjs). Four graders condemned a build that CARRIES the fix, because `merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1 both for a genuine non-ancestor and for a shallow graft: check-rv-sleeve-live.mjs leg 4 (dead(), exit 1, 'no RV outcome row from this build is real'), tra2407-fold-scope-verify.mjs deployVerdict (MISSING, exit 2 UNDEPLOYED), tra3057-verify.mjs leg 1 (a bare `catch { contains = false }` — it had NO cannot-tell state at all), and tra2342-interlock-live-check.mjs's THREE LIVE arms ('Deploy it before arming', against a build already carrying the interlock). These fail CLOSED, so nothing shipped that should not have — the cost is a re-derivation plus a gate people learn to route around, which is how TRA-3678 spent six sessions as a red pin nobody believed. TWO things are graded per subject: the ROUTING (`--ancestry-probe` drives the subject's OWN decision function, not the shared grader) and the EXIT CODE (the subject runs END-TO-END inside the graft against an out-of-process fixture host and must exit non-green AND print `blind-shallow`). That marker is load-bearing: three of the four exit 3 on an unreachable host too, so exit code alone passes on a network blind — the first cut of this harness scored 23/23 that way with the fixture server deadlocked behind spawnSync, and ARM 0d now pins it. Controlled in BOTH directions: every grafted arm has a complete-clone twin that must still ANSWER, and a genuine non-ancestor there must still read ABSENT — 'blind on everything' is the obvious way to fail this fix. Pre-fix rules are quoted from the shipped source at 0270b255 and replayed against the MEASURED graft rc, so a fix arm cannot go green because the repro stopped biting. NOT in pretest, same reason as the other two: it needs a COMPLETE clone.
scripts.//drain:strands: TRA-3541 — the WRITE half of check:strands. The board ruled on 2026-08-13 that hand-draining the blocked+empty recovery-strand cohort every 12h is not a fix; detection was owned and live, the DRAIN was owned by nobody. This does NOT re-implement the cohort predicate: it imports sweep() from check-blocked-empty.mjs and executes the RESTORE-PATCH pair that detector already derives, so the population written to is definitionally the population graded. Per row: POST comment, PATCH {"status":"todo"}, PATCH {"assigneeAgentId":returnOwnerAgentId} — in that order, because assignment is ONE-WAY (afterwards the comment and the status PATCH both 403). ⛔ NEVER `done` (destroys unrun work) and NEVER `blockedByIssueIds` (an empty write-key list reproduces the unroutable born-blocked state); both bans are enforced on the request BODY by gradeWriteBody(), not on the rendered report. Success is verified by RE-READ, never by the 2xx — a PATCH that returns 200 and does not stick reads as FAILED. ⛔ Repair is ASSIGNEE-SCOPED and rank does not lift it, so no single seat can drain the company: a row this seat cannot write is reported FOREIGN and drains from the OWNER's twin arm. Exit 0 VACUOUS (no drainable row existed — NOT a pass, nothing was exercised) / 0 DRAINED / 1 REMAINDER (ineligible or FOREIGN rows nobody is coming for) / 2 FAILED / 3 BLIND. Off-roster+unassigned rows and shape-2 rows are ACKNOWLEDGED: printed in full every fire, but they do not colour the exit, because both classes have a named owner and a daily red gets tuned out. The carve-out is a RULE (off-roster assignee), never an identifier list, so it expires by itself.
scripts.//check:phantom-rest: TRA-2422 — a non-terminal leaf with NO live continuation path. ⛔ TRA-3604 — a MONITOR IS NOT A ROUTINE. `monitorNextCheckAt` and its five siblings live on the ISSUE ROW, a different table, and they are the live path for 32 of the 231 non-terminal leaves (27 of 62 `in_review`) on 2026-08-13. Any sweep that resolves leaves against the routines table alone reads every one of them as unmonitored — a false-positive source ~5x the real signal. This check reads them off the LIST route (which carries all six), and ⛔ their ABSENCE IS SILENT, so key PRESENCE across the swept population is asserted and its loss is BLIND, never a page of findings. ⛔⛔ A FIRED MONITOR SELF-CLEARS: `monitorNextCheckAt` goes null, `monitorLastTriggeredAt` is stamped, `updatedAt` moves ~50ms and nothing else changes — the residue is BYTE-IDENTICAL to a leaf that was never monitored, and no wake, recovery action or `missing_disposition` follows. Calling that PHANTOM_REST prescribes the WRONG REPAIR: PHANTOM_REST says 'arm the monitor that was promised', but on TRA-3436 (fired 08-13T13:30:04Z, 1 attempt) the fire was already SPENT and arming a second one would have been wrong — the repair was to run the grade it should have produced. Hence FIRED_MONITOR_NO_DISPOSITION, its own class with its own repair sentence. ⛔ `monitorLastTriggeredAt` ALONE IS NOT THE TEST: a monitor that fired and RE-ARMED carries both fields and is resting (future `nextCheckAt` wins), and a fired BACKSTOP behind a still-open primary is legitimate rest — 4 of the 5 measured class-B leaves were healthy (TRA-2631/TRA-3104 behind pending cards, TRA-2305/TRA-2937 behind live linked routines). The discriminator is not 'did it fire', it is 'is a primary path still open', so this class is reached only after all six paths say no. ⛔ A 6h GRACE WINDOW (`--fire-grace-hours`) IS LOAD-BEARING: the first live run flagged TRA-3496 **132 seconds** after its fire, i.e. faulted an assignee for not answering a wake delivered two minutes earlier. Fires inside the window are FIRED_IN_FLIGHT, a path, not a strand; the real strands measured were 2–11 DAYS old. ⛔ The A/D/B/C census is PRINTED AT EVERY VERDICT INCLUDING CLEAN — before TRA-3604 the report published findings with no denominator, so '5 spent monitors' and '31 leaves never monitored at all' could not be told apart and neither could be rated.
scripts.//check:routine-dispatch: TRA-2331 — grades the claim check:phantom-rest MAKES. That check clears a leaf as monitored on `active` + `enabled` + a FUTURE `nextRunAt`, and ⛔ `nextRunAt` IS A PROMISE, NOT A RECORD: it is recomputed from the cron and moves forward whether or not the fire ever dispatched, so a routine whose every dispatch is failing reads byte-for-byte identical to a healthy one. The discriminator is the run history. Reads the LIST route only — ⛔ that route OMITS the `recentRuns` key entirely (absent, not []) so `(r.recentRuns || []).length === 0` brands the whole company never-dispatched; it DOES carry `lastRun`, which is the tail verdict in one call. Exit 0 clean / 1 per-routine findings / 2 FLEET (spans the roster — ONE platform condition, do NOT file a ticket per routine) / 3 blind. Zero graded rows is BLIND, never clean. ⛔ TRA-3487 — a `failed` tail is now ATTRIBUTED against the durable owner-pause tape (`activity_log` agent.paused/agent.resumed/agent.terminated, read from the platform's Postgres) AT THE FAILURE INSTANT, splitting into OWNER_PAUSED / OWNER_TERMINATED / OWNER_STATE_UNKNOWN. All three stay findings but are HELD OUT of the FLEET test, because FLEET is a claim about the DISPATCHER and per TRA-2871 the usual TRUE cause of a roster-wide burst is that the OWNERS WERE PAUSED — the old banner asserted 'ONE platform condition' unconditionally and so reproduced the TRA-2867/2871 misdiagnosis twice a day. The banner now NAMES its subject, and a roster-wide pause prints an OWNER PAUSE BURST instead. ⛔ Attribution FAILS CLOSED: an unreadable tape, a coverage floor that does not reach the failure, or an `agent.updated` PATCH touching `status` (the platform logs the KEY, never the VALUE, and agent_config_revisions does not track `status` at all) each yield OWNER_STATE_UNKNOWN — never 'the owner was fine'. ⛔ Do NOT read the tape from /api/../activity: its `action` filter is SILENTLY IGNORED and limit=1000 returns 500 rows (~3.4h). ⛔ TRA-3372 — every EXECUTION_ISSUE_ABANDONED row now NAMES the closing actor and the ASSIGNEE AT CLOSE, read from the same platform Postgres as the pause tape (`activity_log` `issue.updated`, which UNLIKE `agent.updated` records the VALUE and a `_previous` block, so status and assignee moves are recoverable exactly). The finding routes to the ROUTINE OWNER, which is the right default — but on the founding run 3 of 4 rows were closed while the issue belonged to SOMEBODY ELSE (the strand recovery had re-homed them first), so the owner had to reconstruct the actor by hand from the activity log before they could answer 'was this intentional?'. ⛔ The assignee at close is REWOUND BACKWARD from the current assignee, because `recovery.*` re-homes WITHOUT logging `assigneeAgentId` and a forward replay therefore reports the ORIGINAL owner — the exact error being fixed. ⛔ The close is the LAST transition INTO the status the DISPATCHER named, never the newest write (TRA-3196 was re-blocked and re-homed 33h after the close its run was graded on). ⛔ The ACTOR is `actor_type`/`actor_id`, NOT `agent_id` — that column is NULL on every system and user write, i.e. on exactly the writes an owner most needs named. Every failure path is UNATTRIBUTED and prints why; an unreadable tape must never read as 'the owner closed it'. ⛔ ALSO REMOVED: the report used to assert 'under `skip_missed` the slots they lost are gone — nothing will replay them'. That is FALSE. `skip_missed` is the CRON catch-up policy and it is not the only path to a fire: measured 2026-08-13, all three TRA-3372 routines missed BOTH their 07-31 and 08-07 on-slot fires and BOTH were replayed OFF-CRON by a restart backlog drain (08-02T00:08Z, 08-11T13:30Z), one of which ran to completion. This check reads the TAIL, not the schedule ledger, so it cannot tell a lost slot from a replayed one. Do not put it back. ⛔ TRA-3603 — a DESIGNED RETRY RUNG'S SKIP IS NOT A BROKEN TAIL. A date-pinned acceptance ladder is commonly built as PRIMARY+RETRY pairs on ONE routine under `skip_if_active`: the primary lands a carrier, and the retry ten minutes later is refused BECAUSE IT LANDED. This check called every one of those a broken dispatch tail, so its false-positive rate rose with how carefully the routine had been designed — the wrong incentive, and it cost a full hand re-derivation of routine `098ce476` (filed as TRA-3601, ruled false positive). The discriminator is an IDENTITY, not proximity: the skipped run's `linkedIssueId` IS the issue that refused the fire, and a sibling trigger's `lastResult` (`Created execution issue <uuid>`, anchored) names the issue IT created — same uuid ⇒ the thing that blocked this fire is provably this routine's own carrier for the slot. ⛔ SCAN `routine.triggers`, NEVER the armed subset: retiring a spent one-shot arm is the standing remedy for the zombie 2027 `nextRunAt` that check:spent-oneshot files, so the covering PRIMARY is usually `enabled:false` by the time anyone looks (it was on `098ce476`) — reading `armedTriggers()` here fails on the founding fixture and works LESS well the better the owner's hygiene. ⛔ THE LABEL IS NOT THE INSTRUMENT: `t.label` says "RETRY of the 14:15Z slot (no-op if it landed)" and it is prose — a self-colliding routine can carry the word RETRY and a correct one can carry no label — so it is REPORTED and never DECIDES. ⛔ `coalescedIntoRunId` is still never read (Trap 3b, stamped on both branches). ⛔ A WINDOW IS REQUIRED (`--retry-cover-window-min`, default 180) or a STUCK CARRIER buys permanent silence: an issue that never closes matches the identity on every future slot, and a whole cohort collapsing into skips against one wedged carrier is the REAL self-collision this check exists to catch. Fails CLOSED everywhere — unparseable `lastResult`, absent `linkedIssueId`, unreadable `linkedIssue.status`, or an out-of-window fire all leave the row a DISPATCH_SKIPPED finding, because trading this check's false positives for a false negative on the one state it owns is not a fix. Coverage that DIED (carrier `blocked`/`cancelled`) is its own state DISPATCH_SKIPPED_CARRIER_ABANDONED — still a finding, held OUT of FLEET on the EXECUTION_ISSUE_ABANDONED reasoning. ⛔ SUPPRESSED ROWS ARE PRINTED IN FULL at every verdict INCLUDING CLEAN, with the sibling trigger, the carrier, its status and the gap: a suppression nobody can see is one nobody can audit, and this check's whole history is states that read identically in pass and fail.
scripts.//check:carrier-dispatch: TRA-3529 — the NEXT link after check:routine-dispatch. That one grades the DISPATCH TAIL (did the fire produce a run?); this one grades what happens AFTER a successful dispatch: was anybody ever woken on the issue that run created? ⛔⛔ RUN `status` MEASURES ISSUE CLOSURE, NOT EXECUTION — a run sits at `issue_created` until its linked issue reaches a terminal status, and bb11cef4's run flipped to `completed` at the exact instant a sweep closed TRA-3513 BY HAND, no work in between. So `issue_created` (which is in the sibling's RUN_SUCCESS set, correctly, for its own subject) and `completed` both say nothing about whether the order was executed. The discriminator is `issue.startedAt` — the platform's record of a CHECKOUT — and ⛔ it is NOT `assigneeAgentId` (873 of 877 carriers carry one; the routine propagates it correctly) and ⛔ NOT `zero comments` (TRA-3529's stated discriminator, which HEALS WITHOUT A DISPATCH the moment a sweep closing the carrier writes a comment on the way past — a lagging proxy that fails toward CLEAN). ⛔⛔ TRAP: `lastRun.linkedIssue` on the LIST route serves SIX keys (id/identifier/priority/status/title/updatedAt) and `startedAt` IS NOT AMONG THEM, so reading it there brands all 197 carriers never-dispatched — this check FANS OUT to GET /api/issues/{id} and exits BLIND on an absent key. ⛔⛔ TRAP: routine status is NOT filtered — 163 of 197 carriers sit on ARCHIVED routines because a one-shot's own prose orders it to archive itself as step 1, so the `active`-only population that is right for the sibling check would hide 83% of carriers INCLUDING the self-archiving deploy trains that are the urgent case. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 SYSTEMIC with the subject NAMED / 3 blind. ⛔ A pile of findings on ONE assignee is that agent's QUEUE, not a dispatcher fault: measured 2026-08-13, the same agent's MANUALLY-created issues starved at 67% vs 62% for routine-spawned ones while every other assignee sat at ~0% regardless of origin, so the variable is queue depth and the founding cohort only looked routine-specific because it was selected routine-only. Only a spread across the roster leaves the dispatcher as the remaining subject. CARRIER_CANCELLED_UNWORKED (a deliberate retirement) stays a finding but is held OUT of the systemic test so retired routines cannot put a permanent floor under the verdict. ⛔ Grades ONE carrier per routine (the newest), so a worked newest carrier HIDES an abandoned older one — a NAMED blind spot, printed every run, not a silent cap.
scripts.//check:slot-loss: TRA-3713 — the THIRD link, and the one none of the others can reach: not whether a fire produced a run (check:routine-dispatch), nor whether anybody was woken (check:carrier-dispatch), nor whether the commit is live now (check:deploy-train-window), but WHEN the fire happened relative to the slot it was for. Carrier `e7ccfe59` was due 2026-08-13T21:50Z, did not fire, and was replayed by the 00:21Z restart drain 2h31m late — into a window whose embargo reasoning had already expired. Every instrument above read that as healthy. ⛔⛔ THE INTENDED SLOT IS NOT READABLE AFTER THE FACT: `nextRunAt` has already rolled forward (to 2027 on a one-shot), and nothing on the routine, trigger or run records the slot the fire was FOR. It is RE-DERIVED by evaluating the cron BACKWARDS from `triggeredAt` in the trigger's own timezone (scripts/lib/cron-slot.mjs, unit-tested by check:cron-slot). ⛔ THE TIMEZONE IS PART OF THE ANSWER — the fleet mixes ET and UTC triggers, and a UTC-only evaluator is wrong by 4h, which is the same magnitude as the lateness being measured, so the error reads as a different lateness rather than as a bug. ⛔⛔ "THE NEAREST SLOT" IS THE WRONG RULE AND IT ERASES THE DEFECT: on a WEEKLY cron a replay more than half a week late is nearer to the NEXT slot, so nearest-slot laundered three real 3d17h losses (`81928e50`/`a986323e`/`f28ea628`, all replayed by the 08-11T13:30Z drain) into harmless "early" fires. The scheduler already records the answer — `trigger.nextRunAt` still pointing AT a slot proves that slot was never consumed, so the fire belongs to a PAST one. A future slot is admissible ONLY once nextRunAt has moved BEYOND it. ⛔⛔ THE CREATION FLOOR IS LOAD-BEARING: a cron evaluated backwards past the routine's own `createdAt` invents a slot every time, and `618de42d` read "72h late" for a Monday two days before it existed — an accusation manufactured out of calendar arithmetic that looks exactly like a real missed weekly slot. ⛔ A fire attributable to NO slot (`d038b618`: dispatched while its only slot was still armed, created after the previous one) is SLOT_UNATTRIBUTABLE, its own state — reporting it as "24h early" or "8735h late" would be inventing a number in order to have one. ⭐ THE FAIL THRESHOLD IS NOT A CONSTANT: where a carrier declares its window as data (the ```deploy-order `deadline` TRA-3533 already mandates) the check grades against THAT — WINDOW_EXPIRED (exit 5, the incident: it ran on reasoning that had already expired) vs SLOT_LOST_WINDOW_HELD. The numeric band (on-time <= 300s, fail >= 60m) is the FALLBACK for undeclared windows and is two-sided on purpose, with DRIFT reported and never a finding, because a band that fires on ordinary scheduler jitter is muted within a week. ⛔⛔ A RESTART DRAIN IS ONE EVENT, NOT N FINDINGS — fires clustering inside 120s are reported as one RESTART_DRAIN with its members listed, or the report prescribes 13 repairs for one process gap. ⛔ ARCHIVED ROUTINES ARE IN THE POPULATION (the self-archiving deploy trains are the urgent case; `e7ccfe59` is archived). ⛔ NAMED BLIND SPOT, printed every run: the list route carries ONE run per routine, so an on-time newest fire HIDES an older lost slot. ⛔ Exclusions are printed with counts by cause at EVERY verdict including CLEAN, and zero graded rows is BLIND, never clean. 0 clean / 1 SLOT_LOST / 2 usage / 3 BLIND / 4 UNGRADED (a deploy train whose slot could not be established — the urgent class unmeasurable is NOT the urgent class fine) / 5 WINDOW_EXPIRED.
scripts.//check:cron-slot: TRA-3713 — unit controls for the backward cron evaluator that check:slot-loss stands on. Pins the two pre-registered rows, the ET-vs-UTC divergence, both DST edges (a 02:00 slot on 2026-03-08 does not exist and is never invented; an ambiguous 01:00 on 2026-11-01 resolves to the FIRST occurrence), the refusals (named months, macros, dom+dow both restricted), and the four attribution rules. In pretest: it is pure and ~250ms.
scripts.//check:deploy-build: TRA-3695 — the DEPLOY'S OWN build command, in front of `main`, blocking. `070a188a` reached origin/main with a hard TS error and EIGHT commits landed on top of it, every one un-deployable, until a live deploy to the money host was the thing that noticed — bqb1 was then bisected forward commit-by-commit and briefly served two off-tip mid-train builds. ⭐ THE DEFECT IS AN ASYMMETRY, NOT A MISSING CHECKER: the ADVISORY check (lint) already ran pre-deploy and is explicitly non-blocking, while the BLOCKING one (`pnpm build`) ran only at deploy time. CI compiles the packages but runs ON push to main, which is AFTER the commit is on the branch the deploy pulls from — a detector behind the branch, which is what we already had. ⛔ `tsc -b --force` TYPE-CHECKS THE `.test.ts` FILES, so a test file breaks the BUILD without ever running: "tests pass" is NOT evidence, and neither is `pnpm typecheck`, whose project graph is not the graph `packages/server` compiles. This gate therefore runs NO PROXY — it PARSES the deploy's build script out of package.json and runs those segments verbatim, and reads BLIND (3) rather than guessing if the shape changes. ⛔ WHICH command the deploy runs is not knowable from this repo: render.yaml pins `web:build` while the live bqb1 log prints `[render-build]`, and they are NOT the same chain (`render-build` hardcodes four packages, `web:build` globs five — `packages/agents` is in the glob and not the list). So the gate grades the UNION of both and does not have to be right about which the dashboard holds; a render.yaml re-pointed at a third script reads BLIND. ⛔ THE SUBJECT IS THE COMMIT, NEVER THE WORKING TREE — built in a throwaway `git worktree` with node_modules junctioned in. Grading the tree in place is wrong in BOTH directions: an unstaged fix passes a broken commit (the exact failure this closes), and an unrelated dirty file fails a clean one — and a gate that is red for reasons the author did not cause gets `--no-verify`'d on day one, which is the same end state as no gate. ~70s. ⛔ BLIND REFUSES THE PUSH TOO: "could not check" and "checked and it is fine" must never share an exit code. 0 clean / 1 BROKEN (the incident) / 2 usage / 3 BLIND; precedence BLIND > BROKEN > CLEAN. ⭐ `core.hooksPath` is LOCAL config and is NOT committed, so the hook file is inert until something arms it — that is `prepare` → `hooks:install`, and whether it is actually armed is MEASURED by `--verify-hook`, never assumed. Controls run on LIVE HISTORY, not a synthetic plant: `070a188a` (the real break) must read BROKEN and reproduce the Render log's own `(202,66) error TS18047`, and `1ff4fa7b` (the fix) must read CLEAN — without that second arm a gate hardwired to exit 1 would pass.
scripts.//check:deploy-train-window: TRA-3533 — the residual of TRA-3529, and the OUTCOME leg its sibling structurally cannot reach. check:carrier-dispatch grades whether anybody was WOKEN on a routine's carrier; that is the right question about the queue and the wrong one about the deploy, because a carrier can be picked up promptly and the deploy still be refused, or abandoned entirely and the commit still be live off another path. This grades the OUTCOME: is the ordered commit an ancestor of the bytes bqb1 is executing? ⭐ THE POINT IS THAT IT DOES NOT REQUIRE THE CARRIER TO HAVE BEEN WORKED — a lateness check written INTO the carrier's own prose ("fail loudly if you read this past T") is structurally blind, because it only runs if somebody runs the carrier, which is the exact event whose absence IS the defect. ⛔ A deploy train must carry a machine-readable ```deploy-order block (commit/host/deadline); nothing on the board recorded WHAT was ordered or BY WHEN as data, which is why the 2026-08-13 disposition of TRA-3493/TRA-3511/TRA-3513 had to be a human re-derivation from prose. `deadline` MUST end in Z — crons are evaluated in ET and the windows are written in UTC, and a bare local time is REJECTED, never guessed. ⛔ SATISFIED means the commit is live NOW, not that it was live BY THE DEADLINE: the timing arm needs Render deploy history and reports UNREAD, never OK — on 08-13 both deploys were satisfied hours late by an unrelated path, which is exactly the case a bare pass would hide. ⛔ TWO EXIT CODES FOR TWO STATES, on purpose: 1 STRANDED (deadline passed, commit not live — the incident, the only code that should page) vs 4 UNGRADED (suspected trains carrying no block — a migration backlog). Folding them into one number buries the incident: the first live run flagged 18 suspected and 0 stranded. ⛔ The prose classifier is a HINT with known false positives (TRA-3413 says "if you find yourself about to redeploy bqb1, STOP"; TRA-3398 quotes an embargo) so it reports SUSPECTED, never "defective" — a grader over other people's artefacts fails toward convicting them. Opt out with `<!-- deploy-order: none -->`. ⛔ Default population is carriers fired in the last 7 days keyed on lastRun.triggeredAt, and the excluded count is PRINTED — the unfiltered first run flagged 53 settled July one-shots for lacking a field that did not exist when they were written. An unreadable triggeredAt is INCLUDED, never dropped. ⛔ Same NAMED blind spot as its sibling: ONE carrier per routine, the newest. Exit 0 clean / 1 STRANDED / 2 usage / 3 BLIND / 4 UNGRADED; precedence BLIND > STRANDED > UNGRADED > CLEAN. Live path proven both directions on TRA-3536 (a real fixture issue whose ordered commit is the SHA ALREADY LIVE, so obeying it is a strict no-op). ⭐ THE TIMING ARM IS NOW REAL AND IS THE POINT: `SATISFIED` is live NOW, and `on_time`/`late` is live BY THE DEADLINE. With RENDER_API_KEY + RENDER_SERVICE_ID set it reads Render's deploy history, binds it to the box by LIVE-SHA IDENTITY (the block names the onrender host `tradingai-bqb1` while the Render service's own name is `TradingAI-`, so a name lookup returns []), and grades whether a SERVED deploy carrying the ordered commit finished before the deadline. A missed window exits 5 LATE — not 1, because nothing is stranded, and not 0, because the window a one-shot exists to hit was missed. It fails to UNREAD and NEVER to LATE on: history that starts after the deadline, a pre-deadline deploy whose commit this checkout does not know, or nothing in the window carrying the commit — a grader over other people's deploys fails toward convicting them. build_failed/canceled deploys never count as "it was live by then". Precedence BLIND > STRANDED > LATE > UNGRADED > CLEAN.

Exit 0 clean / 1 findings with coverage intact / 2 COVERAGE_LOST (a routine whose only arms are spent) / 3 blind. scripts.//check:fix-live: TRA-2644 — 'is MY fix in the bytes being executed', which check:deploy-drift CANNOT answer. Ancestry of --commit against the live SHA, NOT drift: drift measures the whole company's merge rate against one box, so it is routinely non-zero on a weekday and a grading gate keyed to it never opens. Requires --commit (no default: a default is how a grader confirms the wrong fix). --window-start=<ISO> adds the arm a point-in-time SHA read cannot have — every build that held `live` across the window must contain the commit, because a rollback mid-session makes that session's EOD row a mixture of two writers. Exit 0 PRESENT / 1 ABSENT / 2 CONTAMINATED (window spans a build without the fix) / 3 BLIND. scripts.//check:boot-arm-repairs: TRA-3810 — the DETECTION half of the TRA-2649 write-path arm. `check:boot-arm` grades the arm's STATE (eligible + drift); this grades whether anyone TRIED to demote it. Bound to `bootArmRepairLedger` (durable, append-only under DATA_DIR), never to `bootArmWriteRepairs` — that counter is a since-boot delta whose `0` reads identically for "clean" and "never exercised" and which a redeploy zeroes, so an alarm on it pins OFF exactly when it matters. Exit 0 CLEAN (zero attempts over a MEASURED window ≥ --min-window-days) / 1 ATTEMPTS (the alarm) / 2 NOT MEASURED (sound instrument, window absent or under the floor — vacuous, never a pass) / 3 BLIND (ephemeral DATA_DIR, swallowed appends, no hydrate, ineligible arm, pre-TRA-3810 build, or unreachable probe). Precedence ATTEMPTS > BLIND > NOT MEASURED > CLEAN: a positive is true whatever the coverage is, so blindness can never demote a real live-money demotion attempt into a plumbing complaint.
scripts.//check:boot-arm-repairs:acks: TRA-3852 — `retentionDays` is 180 and the grade was `attempts > 0 → exit 1`, so ONE settled event (the 2026-08-17 TRA-3833 full-settings-save) pinned the alarm ON for half a year and the sixth recurrence of the boot-arm family would have arrived inside that noise. `scripts/boot-arm-repair-acks.json` clears ONE event from the exit code and nothing else: matched on exact `at` + `origin` + `repaired` set + `bodyFields.length` (a new attempt from the same writer has a different timestamp and still exits 1), and only while its `fixCommit` is an ANCESTOR OF THE SERVING COMMIT — roll the fix back and the ack goes VOID and the event alarms again, which the old unconditional exit 1 could not have distinguished. Undeterminable ancestry applies no ack. Acked events are still printed in full every fire, tagged with the issue that settled them, and the resulting pass is the distinct verdict ATTEMPTS-ACKNOWLEDGED (exit 0), never CLEAN. Because that pass asserts an ABSENCE of NEW attempts it falls through the blindness and window-floor gates, so a blind or unmeasured instrument can never reach it. `--no-acks` grades as if nothing were acknowledged — that is the positive control.

scripts.//tra2906:rebuild-cash-flow: TRA-2906 — one-time v1→v2 migration of tradier-cash-flow.<env>.json, which is what makes the broker-fee reclassification reachable at all. The v1 record persists ONE signed number per date and discards the event type, so removing `fee` from a set only affects events NOT YET SEEN: the fees already folded into stored totals stay folded in, permanently mis-signed. ⛔ THE SCRIPT DOES NOT WRITE WHAT THE BROKER RETURNS. Before writing it re-derives the legacy totals from the fetched events under the OLD rule and asserts they reproduce the stored netByDate date-for-date; only then does it apply the new rule, so the classification change is provably the only variable. That control is the whole point — a short or `limit`-truncated fetch would otherwise write a v2 record missing months of deposits, and ⛔ A DELETED DEPOSIT DOES NOT LOOK LIKE AN ERROR, IT LOOKS LIKE A GREAT TRADING DAY. `netByDate` is the only surviving record of those deposits; there is no second copy. Mismatch in EITHER direction refuses. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT — it prints the measured per-date P&L shift so the expected move is MEASURED before shipping rather than asserted from a stale claim. Must run ON THE HOST (needs TRADIER_API_TOKEN + TRADIER_ACCOUNT_ID and the data dir). Exit 0 clean/applied · 1 REFUSED · 2 usage · 3 BLIND · 4 NOOP (already v2).
